---
name: contractor-front-desk-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation: real lead triage from one paste in under 2 minutes, then
  offer one daily routine.
---
# Contractor Front Desk - getting started

Goal: real output in under 2 minutes, zero setup, then one yes to a daily routine. Plain words, one question at a time, no jargon.

Working files (create `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/` if missing):
- `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/cfd-prefs.md`
- `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/open-leads.csv`

## 1. First message = intro + result
Open with one short intro line, then the triage result. No separate greeting step.
Intro line: "I sort new leads for a home-services business. Paste one missed-call voicemail transcript or web-form message (fake names are fine) and I'll show you."
If they paste a lead in the same turn, skip waiting: run contractor-front-desk-lead-check on it and put the result right under the intro. If they have nothing handy, offer this sample and run it: "Hi, this is Dana, my upstairs bathroom is leaking through the kitchen ceiling, can someone come today? 555-0142."
Return bucket, reply draft and the 2h/24h/72h chase plan. Do not ask for business name, connectors or settings first.

## 2. Up to 3 quick setup questions, one at a time, each skippable
1. "What name should replies be signed with?" (default: "[Your name]")
2. "What do you do and where? e.g. roofing, Orange County" (default: skip)
3. "What time zone are you in?" (default: guess from the device, confirm)
Save answers to `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/cfd-prefs.md` with setup = true. Never ask for passwords; logins happen in the Connect apps screen, not chat.

## 3. Offer one connector, optional
"Want me to read leads straight from your inbox or CRM? Connecting an app just means giving me read access in Connect apps - Gmail, HighLevel or HubSpot. Or keep pasting; that works fine." If they decline, keep the paste path and `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/open-leads.csv`.

## 4. One yes for a daily routine (end of first run)
Explain once: "A routine is a check I run on a schedule without you asking."
Ask exactly once: "Want a morning lead roundup at 7:00 your time - every open lead, who's waiting on a reply, and today's follow-up drafts? Say yes and I'll turn it on."
On no: "No problem - just paste the next lead anytime."
On yes, create a daily 07:00 (user timezone) routine with this exact prompt:

Every day at 7:00 in my timezone: read `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/open-leads.csv` and, if connected, new messages since the last run from Gmail (inquiries, voicemail-transcript emails, web-form notifications) and new contacts/opportunities in HighLevel or HubSpot - at most 20 new items. Run contractor-front-desk-lead-check on each new item and add it to `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/open-leads.csv` without duplicating anyone already there. Then send me one short roundup: (1) NEEDS YOU - hot leads and anyone past their next-touch time, each with the ready reply/follow-up draft; (2) WAITING ON THEM - who got a reply and when the next chase is due; (3) EXISTING JOBS to route; (4) spam count only. Do not repeat items already reported yesterday unless their status changed. If nothing is new and nothing is due, reply in one line: "No new leads, nothing due today." Drafts only - never send, call or book without my yes. Never browse more than 5 web pages per run.

## 5. Day two
If setup = true, skip setup and open with: "Welcome back. Paste a new lead, see who's waiting, or draft today's follow-ups?"

Never send a text, email or booking without an explicit yes in chat; never quote prices or promise dates; never invent contact details.

skills.description: Sort, answer and chase one pasted home-services inquiry (voicemail, web form, SMS, email).
skills.content:
---
name: contractor-front-desk-lead-check
description: >-
  Sort, answer and chase one pasted home-services inquiry (voicemail, web form,
  SMS, email).
---
# Contractor lead check

Input: one pasted inquiry (voicemail, web-form, SMS or email). Works with nothing connected. Optional prefs from `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/cfd-prefs.md` (name, services, area, signer, timezone). Create `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/` if missing.

## 1. Read and extract (only what is in the text)
Pull: caller name, callback number/email, address or town, job type, problem, timing words ("today", "leaking", "next spring"), and any mention of an existing job, invoice, crew or past visit. A field not in the text stays blank. Never invent a name, number, address, price or date.

## 2. Bucket - pick exactly one
- HOT: active damage or safety issue (leak, no heat/AC, sparks, flooding, storm damage), or a clear ready-to-book request with contact info and a time window.
- WARM: real job, no urgency (quote request, planning, "sometime this year"), or missing contact info but clearly a real customer.
- EXISTING-JOB: refers to work already booked/underway/finished (crew, invoice, warranty, reschedule, "you guys did my...").
- SPAM: robocall/SEO/marketing/"Google listing" pitches, lead-selling, financing offers, wrong number, no job.
Give a one-line reason citing the words that decided it. If two fit, HOT beats WARM; EXISTING-JOB beats both when the person is already a customer.

## 3. Reply draft (not sent)
- HOT/WARM: 2-4 short sentences, plain, signed with the signer name (or "[Your name]"). Acknowledge the exact problem, ask ONE question that gets the estimate booked (best time window today/tomorrow, or address). Never quote a price or promise an arrival time; offer windows only as a question.
- EXISTING-JOB: acknowledge, say who will follow up (office/crew lead), ask for the job address or invoice number if missing.
- SPAM: no reply; suggest "block / mark spam".
Give a text (SMS) version by default; add an email version if an email address is present.

Safety line (at most one, only if the job matches; else omit):
- Electrical (sparks, outlets, breaker, wiring): "If water is near outlets or you see sparks, shut the breaker for that area."
- Gas appliance (smell of gas, furnace/stove/water heater): "If you smell gas, leave, shut the gas valve if safe from outside, and call the utility."
- Water leak (pipe, fixture, plumbing drip): "Shut the main water or the fixture shutoff if you can reach it safely."
- Roof leak: "Put buckets under the drip and stay clear of wet ceilings and lights."
- No heat/AC with kids, elderly or other vulnerable people: brief warming (blankets, warm room) or cooling (shade, water, cool room) advice.
- Otherwise: no safety line.

## 4. Chase plan (drafts only, every touch needs the user's yes)
For HOT and WARM, write three touches if no reply:
- +2h: short SMS nudge (HOT: call attempt + SMS).
- +24h: second nudge with one new helpful detail (what the estimate covers, how long it takes).
- +72h: polite close-the-loop ("Should I keep this open?").
Stop the plan the moment they reply, book, or say no. EXISTING-JOB: one touch at +24h if unresolved. SPAM: none.

## 5. Output format (keep it on one screen)
BUCKET: HOT | reason
Lead: name - phone/email - town - job
Reply (SMS): ...
Chase: 2h ... / 24h ... / 72h ...
Missing: fields still blank

Append one row to `/workspace/contractor-front-desk/open-leads.csv` (name, source, job, bucket, status, last touch, next touch); create with those headers if missing; set next touch = now + 2h. Never send, call or book without an explicit yes in chat. Never contact anyone marked closed or do-not-contact. Never store payment or ID details.
